concept.reason: Actual museum skeleton and scale-bearing taxon-specific foot bone plus published measurements suffice.

scope: Original low heavy moa body and exceptionally stout short lower legs; complete animal, subsequent pool not frozen72.

scale.measured_source: Worthy and Holdaway1994 Ngarua Cave site3 specimen recovered by M.Endres, cranial voucherS27795. Not AM LB5950 or TePapaS.040230.
scale.height_status: Estimated chosen neck posture, not a measured complete animal. NZBirdsOnline120cm is LENGTH, not shoulder or skull height.
scale.photo_scale: TePapa S.040230 tarsometatarsus photo3cm bar; different specimen. Approx photographic bone length~0.22m supports proportions, not exact caliper measurement.

diagnostic_targets: Broad low heavy oval feathered trunk, no visible or vestigial wings.
Exceptionally short stout tarsometatarsi and broad feet, unlike long slender ostrich legs.
Long thick forward-curving neck, small rounded head and sturdy pointed decurved bill; no casque or giant duck bill.
Three forward clawed toes plus small hind toe per foot, no ostrich two-toed feet or webbing.
Restrained shaggy feather contour, scaly bare lower legs, no fan tail.
Thighs covered by bulky body, readable negative spaces between stout legs and toes.
uncertainties: Living soft contour, posture and precise plumage pattern/colors are inferred; feather evidence permits variation, not a fixed proven painted pattern.
AM LB5950 is mounted museum skeleton; mount pose and missing ribs do not define exact living silhouette.
No claim that limb measurements, separate tarsometatarsus and skeleton photo are same individual.
Tring photo caption says heavy-footed but filename says eastern-moa; it is excluded from production reference set to avoid ambiguous identity.
acceptance: Original heavy low body with very stout short lower legs preserved.
No wing objects, no ostrich feet; curved neck not giant upright Dinornis.
Four exactGLB views, two reproducible builds then independentQA.
